prerequisites: Defining basic concepts, theories, and methods in the fundamental field of engineering sciences; their adequate use in professional communication;

learning_outcomes.text: Defines the fundamental concepts of polymeric materials, classifies the main categories of polymers;
Explains the relationship between macromolecular structure, morphology, and physical-mechanical properties of polymers;
Compares polymer characterization methods (spectroscopic, thermal, mechanical, morphological);
Differentiates thermoplastics from thermosetting polymers and elastomers by structure and properties;
Explains the general principles of polymer processing and the factors influencing the quality of finished products;
Describes the main processing methods: extrusion, injection, thermoforming, and blow molding of polymers;
Interprets the results of polymer material tests according to current standards;
Evaluates modern sustainability solutions: biopolymers, recycling, polymeric composite materials;
Applies selection criteria for polymeric materials based on specific application requirements.
Uses digital tools for simulating processing methods and predicting the properties of polymeric materials;
Plans and executes physical-mechanical, thermal, and rheological characterization tests for polymers;
Operates laboratory equipment for 3D printing and mechanical testing of polymers;
Optimizes processing parameters to obtain products with desired properties;
Critically evaluates the quality of polymeric products, identifies processing defects and their causes;
Selects appropriate polymeric materials for specific applications, considering economic and sustainability aspects;
Interprets diagrams, curves, and results for the complete characterization of polymers.
Respects ethical principles, norms, and values in the responsible use of polymeric materials, by promoting sustainable solutions and reducing environmental impact;
Integrates into multidisciplinary teams in the materials industry and applies effective collaboration techniques with specialists in chemistry, materials engineering, and product design;

Continuously informs and documents oneself about developments in the field of polymers, new biodegradable materials, and recycling technologies, through the adequate use of continuous learning methods;

Develops complete projects for the selection, characterization, and processing of polymeric materials, demonstrating autonomy in technical decision-making and responsibility for environmental and societal impact;
Promotes circular economy principles in the use of polymers and contributes to the development of innovative solutions for the sustainability of the polymeric materials industry.

syllabus_topics: Modern trends and sustainability: biopolymers, recycling, polymeric composite materials
3-point static bending testing of polymeric materials
4-point static bending testing of polymeric materials
Combined tensile and shear stress testing

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory activity (lab reports and laboratory colloquium)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Integer grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of the minimum learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of the associated study credits. All laboratory works must be completed, allowing only one outstanding laboratory work to be made up.
